subject: Next steps: Hosting path, compliance evidence & SLA split for MediSys
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Liza Chen <liza.chen@medisys.com>, security@medisys.com <security@medisys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap — Hosting paths, compliance evidence, and SLA split

Hi Liza / MediSys security team,

Thanks for the time today — we covered the primary constraints that will determine whether MediSys goes Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, or a Private VPC/on-prem setup. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of options and drivers:
- Hosted API: fastest to production, supports token-level cost controls and region routing. Good if PHI is minimal and the BAA + SOC2 evidence meets your security checklist.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools under your tenancy with stronger isolation and predictable throughput. Appropriate when you want guaranteed throughput and a contractual SLA tie (monthly commit).
- Private VPC / on-prem: full network isolation and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Recommended when your internal auditors require on-prem or strict data residency for PHI.

Compliance asks we discussed (what we will provide):
- SOC 2: concise summary + control mapping (attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf)
- BAA: template and typical redlines; we can begin the NDA/BAA review in parallel with technical work
- Audit evidence: access logs, tokenization patterns, and retention policies — we can provide time-stamped samples and an audit checklist

Action items (owners & timeline):
1) MediSys security to confirm the minimal viable deployment for your pilot (Hosted versus Dedicated) by Tue 24 Aug — Liza (owner).
2) Redwood to send deployment comparison matrix and evidence package by EOD Mon 23 Aug — Marissa (owner). Attachment: deployment-options-matrix.xlsx
3) If MediSys needs Private/VPC onboarding checklist, Redwood will scope network and KMS requirements and send an estimated timeline (3–6 weeks typical) — Sean (owner).
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security folks to walk evidence and network details — propose Wed 25 Aug 11:00 AM ET (meeting link below).

If you confirm the pilot will process PHI under a BAA, we should prioritize the Dedicated path or Private VPC; Hosted can work if data is de-identified and legal signs off.

Meeting link: https://meetings.redwood.ai/kal/medisys-hosting-08-25

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, deployment-options-matrix.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

---
Note: This recap includes suggested SLA split language (see matrix) — open to adjusting the service-level and credit language once we know which path you choose.

From: Liza Chen <liza.chen@medisys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medisys.com <security@medisys.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 08:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Hosting paths, compliance evidence, and SLA split

Thanks Karthik — useful summary. Quick clarifications from the security team: 

1) Data residency: pilot data must remain in US regions only. Is the Hosted API able to guarantee US-only processing (no fallback to other regions) and can you include that in the BAA?
2) Encryption: confirm encryption at rest with customer-provided KMS is available for Dedicated and Private VPC options. For Hosted, we need to understand key custody options.
3) Audit timeline: our auditors want a sample of a seven-day access log extract and an example of SOC2 control mappings against an external registry.

We will aim to decide on the pilot path by Tue 24 Aug but want the evidence packet before then. Also please include a short note about incident response timelines for Dedicated vs Hosted (RTO/RPO expectations).

Liza Chen
Head of Security Programs, MediSys Health
liza.chen@medisys.com

On a side note, are you able to share reference customers who used Dedicated for a PHI pilot?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liza Chen <liza.chen@medisys.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Hosting paths, compliance evidence, and SLA split

Hi Liza — thanks for the clear list. Short answers inline and next attachments.

1) US-only processing: Yes — Hosted API requests can be pinned to US regions and we can add a contractual clause in the BAA guaranteeing processing within US data centers for the pilot. We will also document fallback behavior (no cross-region fallback for your pilot).

2) Encryption & KMS:
- Dedicated & Private VPC: we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and HSM-backed keys.
- Hosted: standard deployment uses Redwood-managed keys, but for enterprise pilots we support a dedicated key wrap where keys are customer-owned in your cloud KMS and we perform envelope encryption. We'll include the options and technical notes in the packet.

3) Audit evidence: attached is a 7-day sample access log extract (redacted), and the SOC2 control mapping summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). We'll also include the RFC-style mapping to the typical external registry used by auditors.

Incident response timeline (high level):
- Hosted API: P1 response target 1 hour for triage, full incident report within 72 hours; limited SLA credits for multi-tenant Hosted in pilot tier.
- Dedicated: 30-minute P1 triage, detailed post-incident RCA within 48 hours; SLA credits tied to reserved capacity commitments.
- Private VPC: response SLAs can be contractually adjusted depending on on-prem support add-ons.

References: we can connect you to a current Dedicated pilot customer (name & reference will follow with their permission).

I attached: deployment-options-matrix.xlsx and redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (see links above). If you want, Sean can follow up with the network/KMS checklist.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Customer Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Hosting paths, compliance evidence, and SLA split

Liza — thanks, and appreciated the fast turnaround. Quick confirmation of next steps: 

- Marissa will send the packet (sent) and Sean will prepare the network/KMS checklist for Private/VPC.
- Please confirm preferred time for the technical deep-dive on Wed 25 Aug 11:00 AM ET or propose an alternate; I'll lock the invite after your confirmation.
- I'll open a parallel DocuSign thread for the BAA template so legal can start redlines while we do the technical work.

If you confirm pilot = PHI under BAA, our recommended default path is Dedicated for the first 90-day pilot (predictable throughput + better contractual SLAs). We can assess Private VPC for full production after audit sign-off.

I'll follow up with a short mutual action plan with owners once you confirm the pilot path.
